name: Montana

notes: No state sales tax; a few resort towns levy local resort taxes (not included).
gaps: Montana has no state or local general sales tax.

Ten resort areas levy a 3% resort tax on lodging, restaurants and bars, destination recreation and "luxuries" (recorded as "meals_local" and "resort_local"); which goods count as luxuries is set locally and is not applied to the other categories here.

Resort areas that are unincorporated (Big Sky, Cooke City, Craig, Gardiner, St. Regis, Wolf Creek) are recorded on the Census CDP of the same name, whose boundary may differ from the resort district's.
The two Department of Revenue pages disagree: revenuefiles.mt.gov lists Whitefish, Craig and Gardiner, which mtrevenue.gov omits; the longer list is used.
